submitted.rationale: Of the three compositions measured, index 19 (Cr0.378Sb0.622) had the highest EQE, 0.0292%. EQE rose steadily with Sb content: 0.016% at Sb 0.285, 0.027% at Sb 0.49, 0.029% at Sb 0.62. This fits MEGNet's prediction that Sb-rich Cr-Sb-O phases have smaller band gaps (Cr3Sb5O16 about 0.88 eV) and so absorb the 2.1 eV light well.

rejected.reason: The 1:1 CrSbO4 composition gave a lower EQE, 0.0267%.
The Cr-rich composition had the lowest EQE, 0.0162%.

consultations.verdict: Support: rutile CrSbO4 predicted HSE gap ~1.98 eV (<2.1 eV illumination, so absorbs) and near hull (0.065 eV/atom). Index 14 (Sb 0.49) is closest to the 1:1 stoichiometry.

Mild support: Cr-rich Cr5Sb3O16 is near hull (0.082 eV/atom) with ~1.98 eV gap (absorbs 2.1 eV light); Sb-rich Cr3Sb5O16 is less stable (0.107). Probing the Cr-rich side (index 8, Sb 0.285) to bracket the 1:1 result.

Support: Cr3Sb5O16 predicted gap 0.88 eV (strong absorption at 2.1 eV), and the measured EQE rose from the Cr-rich side (0.016 at Sb 0.285) to 1:1 (0.027 at Sb 0.49). Extrapolating toward Sb-rich, I'm measuring index 19 (Sb 0.622).
